summary: Pinegrove Health - priority-routing fallthrough causing throttling, partial failover, and customer-impact action plan
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported widespread timeouts and degraded throughput for high-priority requests routed from Pinegrove Health's private placement (VPC peered) beginning ~2026-03-10T02:05UTC. Traffic that should have been routed to reserved dedicated pool nodes experienced priority fallthrough to shared capacity and an automated fallback to a quantized model variant. Impact included elevated 5xxs, streaming truncation for long-form clinical notes, duplicated completions from retry amplification, and unexpected invoice delta for March billing window.

Impact:
- ~18% of Pinegrove traffic saw increased P50 latency from 120ms to 1.6s and P99 spikes to 8s for a 2 hour window.
- Several inference streams truncated clinical transcripts mid-response (multiple customers reported >50 truncated transcripts).
- Estimated billing exposure: ~+$8.6k due to duplicate completions and fallback to more expensive burst capacity.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peered) with Dedicated capacity (3x A100 pools) in eu-west-1.
- Model variant: primary redwood-open-l2-16b pinned by customer, fallback redwood-quant-16b-int8.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer issues high-priority inference requests with priority header X-Redwood-Priority: high.
2) Smart-routing service evaluated routing policy (dedicated pool preferred).
3) Under transient autoscaler decisions, routing policy returned fallthrough route to shared-hosted pool.
4) Shared pool rejected some long-running streams due to kernel-selection mismatch; system triggered fallback to quantized variant which compressed tokens differently, causing partial truncation and duplicate completions on client retry.

Relevant logs and traces:
- Trace IDs: 74c1f2b9.., e93a5d77.. (see attached SRE trace snippets).
- LB logs show 504s at 2026-03-10T02:06:11Z correlating with autoscaler activity.
- Control plane audit: policy-eval v2.14.3 returned "fallthrough" for 3% of requests in window.

Mitigation applied so far:
- 2026-03-10T02:20UTC: temporarily pinned Pinegrove traffic to dedicated pool by customer-config override (manual route pin).
- 2026-03-10T02:35UTC: SRE scaled dedicated reservation +1 GPU set to drain shared pool handoffs.
- 2026-03-10T03:10UTC: rolling restart of smart-routing service with routing policy fix rolled to eu-west.
- Customer notified and given temporary billing credit estimate; committed to follow-up with final reconciliation.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Hypothesis A: Autoscaler oscillation created transient capacity gaps -> routing fallthrough. Evidence: autoscaler logs show three back-to-back scale-in suggestions at 02:04-02:06 with unusually short cooldown.
- Hypothesis B: Routing policy engine regression in v2.14.3 incorrectly classified some high-priority tokens as low-priority due to header parsing change in recent config. Evidence: audit traces show header X-Redwood-Priority dropped in 2.1% of flows when coming through privatelink NAT.
- Hypothesis C: Kernel selection mismatch on shared pool for long sequences caused stream resets and client retries -> duplicate completions. Evidence: runtime logs show kernel fallback events aligned with 504 spikes.
Intermediate findings:
- Confirmed routing policy bug introduced in config merge MR #2375 where a conditional short-circuit for header parsing was added.
- Confirmed autoscaler cooldown tuning contributed to oscillation but did not by itself cause fallthrough; the short-circuit made the policy incorrectly choose fallthrough target during the oscillation window.
- Duplicate completions were amplified by client-side immediate retry behaviour; server-side idempotency token checks were inconsistent for the quantized variant.
Next steps for eng investigation assigned in INT-1124.

root_cause: A recent routing config merge (MR #2375) introduced a short-circuit in header parsing that intermittently dropped priority headers when traffic traversed privatelink/NAT paths. Combined with aggressive autoscaler cooldown settings, the mis-evaluated policy caused priority routing fallthrough to shared capacity. Shared pool kernel-selection mismatches for long-sequence workloads led to streaming resets; client immediate retries without idempotency guards produced duplicate completions and billing exposure.
resolution_summary:
- Reverted the header parsing short-circuit via routing hotfix (PR #2490) and rolled to eu-west.
- Applied conservative autoscaler cooldown settings in dedicated pools to reduce oscillation risk.
- Enforced idempotency token validation consistently across primary and quantized variants to reduce duplicate completions.
- Provided Pinegrove with provisional billing credit estimate and will finalize after full reconciliation.
Resolution status: mitigations applied; monitoring green in eu-west; post-incident follow-up scheduled.
